description: Documentation corpus for this service. One markdown file per surface or concept, in docs/. This index is what search_docs ranks over; read_doc returns a file's contents.

docs.title: Agents
docs.summary: An agent is a definition, not a process: a prompt, a set of tools, a model, and optionally memory. Running it produces a [run](sessions-and-runs.md).
headings: What an agent is made of

docs.title: Assistant
docs.summary: A person's own assistant, by voice or text: the Assistant page with the live mark and push to talk, the assistant system agent, which extends the Main Agent, one thread per person at /api/assistant, turns in any workspace the person belongs to, speech in and out with the workspace's speech models or the browser's own, a spoken yes for a waiting card, one read-only hub_lookup over runs, sessions, spend, budgets, models, agents, notifications and approvals, hub_lookup over every page's records, one-step changes with hub_action behind a card or a spoken yes, a service thread with health tools and service_lookup (users, audit, settings) for administrators, and turns refused with code budget once a limit is used up.

docs.title: Agent inheritance
docs.summary: An agent can extend another: start from its prompt, tools, model and the rest, and declare only what is different. A system agent can be a parent, never a child.
headings: What is inherited and what is not
Setting, changing and pinning the parent
The guard on a parent's change

docs.title: Chat
docs.summary: The front door. Talk to any agent in the workspace directly; no node, no task, no setup.
headings: What you can point it at

docs.title: The CLI
docs.summary: `ah` drives the service from a terminal: the same operations as the dashboard, either in this process or over REST against a backend elsewhere. Command groups for every entity, commands generated from the OpenAPI schema, `ah api` as the raw escape hatch, and a single-file binary for REST mode.
headings: Two ways it reaches the service

docs.title: Declarative files: ah apply
docs.summary: Agents, environments, deployments and memory pools declared in files in a repository; `ah apply` prints a plan (create, update, unchanged, drift, delete) and makes the hub match, recording hub ids in an `ah.lock` so the next apply updates instead of duplicating. Drift detection, `--prune`, `--export` from existing records.

docs.title: Chat channels
docs.summary: Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams and mail are chat channels where agents run in response to inbound messages. Each has bindings from chats to a workspace plus one agent or flow, and a status card showing running state and last error.

docs.title: Connections
docs.summary: An agent that already runs in production, on its own triggers, reporting what it does into this hub. The hub starts nothing and only watches.
headings: When a graph stops to ask

docs.title: Connectors
docs.summary: Services this hub reaches out to: chat channels (Slack, Discord, Teams, mail), git providers (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea), Telegram, issue trackers (Jira, Linear), integrations (Google Workspace, Microsoft Graph), and Blender. The other direction from connections.

docs.title: Containers
docs.summary: Agents can run in-process or in Docker. Container mode isolates a run: its own filesystem view, its own network posture, its own lifetime.

docs.title: Costs
docs.summary: Token and estimated USD spend, broken down by workspace, agent, model or project, with budget caps that are enforced rather than advisory.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.summary: Scheduled agent_task, flow and loop jobs shown as production deployments: a per-run money cap, an environment, and a firing journal that shows whether each firing actually worked.

docs.title: Environments
docs.summary: A named execution profile: mode, image, packages, network policy, limits and plain variables a task, node or scheduled job runs in.

docs.title: Evals
docs.summary: Eval sets, graders and model sweeps: measure whether a prompt change helped instead of guessing. Online evals grade a sample of production runs by alert rule. Any run becomes a case with one button, and a sweep's failed cases can propose a revised prompt to apply as a new agent version.

docs.title: Experiments
docs.summary: A/B experiments between stored versions of an agent's definition: traffic shares, deterministic routing per run or conversation, and a per-arm report of outcomes, cost and online eval scores.
headings: Rollback and new versions during an experiment

docs.title: Flows
docs.summary: A flow is a graph of agents run as one pipeline: nodes do work, edges define order, and the whole thing streams as it goes.

docs.title: Hooks and tool approval
docs.summary: Two ways to put a human, or the operator's own code, in front of a single tool call: hooks run around every call, and the approval gate holds a call until a person says yes.

docs.title: Imported agents
docs.summary: An agent that already exists, already works and has its own dependencies does not need rebuilding here. Import it from its git repository: the hub clones it, checks whether it can run, and adds it to the agent list either way.

docs.title: Installing and running the service
docs.summary: Four ways to run the service, Docker first: the published images for one person (nothing to clone or build), Docker Compose from a checkout, the installer, and by hand. Then configuration, where state lives, upgrading, and what to check when it will not start.
headings: Path A: Docker, from the published images
Path B: Docker Compose from a checkout

docs.title: Instances
docs.summary: An instance is a live copy of an agent: its own state, its own label, its own history. A resident instance is the one Run on an agent's page starts: a process or container of its own that answers its mailbox in several conversations, can take the agent's tasks, and can be published at a public address through the hub. Nodes were folded into instances.

docs.title: Services
docs.summary: An agent kept running as replicas: the desired state (agent, workspace, environment, replicas min and max, concurrency, idle stop, budget, version) a supervisor keeps, and the runner every chat, /v1, widget and Telegram turn goes to so the backend runs no agent.

docs.title: Loops
docs.summary: A loop wraps a [flow](flows.md) and re-runs it, feeding back a reviewer's complaints, until an agent judges the result good enough.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.summary: The catalog of agents, flows and skills published across workspaces: how a thing built in one workspace gets published, cloned and used in another.
headings: Publishing an agent, a flow or a skill
When to reach for a published agent

docs.title: Industry agent kits
docs.summary: A ready set of agents for one line of work, with the connectors it needs and an outcome rubric for each agent, installed into a workspace in one step. Support, finance operations and recruiting ship with the hub.

docs.title: Agent registry
docs.summary: Which agents, flows, skills and MCP servers the hub has across workspaces, who owns each and whether an administrator approved it. With AGENTS_HUB_REGISTRY_REQUIRE_REVIEW on, publishing to the marketplace waits in review until an admin approves, and an approved item whose definition changes goes back to review; with AGENTS_HUB_MCP_ALLOWLIST_ONLY on, a workspace can attach only MCP servers that match an approved entry of the hub-wide catalog, and attached servers that do not match load no tools. The Agent registry page, GET /api/registry and ah mcp catalog.

docs.title: MCP servers
docs.summary: Attach an external Model Context Protocol server as a group of tools: per workspace, classified by the capabilities its operator declares, and gated by the same hooks and approvals the built-in tools use.

docs.title: Memory
docs.summary: Agents have several complementary memory layers, bound to a pool. Core memory blocks are always in the prompt; the rest are ranked and fetched with tools. The pool is assigned per workspace, so the same agent can carry different knowledge in different workspaces. Personal memory is one private pool per user and workspace that the agents share, switched per workspace and per agent.

docs.title: Models
docs.summary: The Models page is the source of truth for which models exist, which are offered, what they cost, and which is default per provider.

docs.title: What this service is
docs.summary: An agent hub: a place to define AI agents, give them tools and memory, and run them, alone or in groups, against real work in a workspace.

docs.title: Page chat
docs.summary: The button in the corner of every page: a chat about the page you are on, holding the records that page is showing.

docs.title: Help
docs.summary: The Help button in the header: the Support agent, for when you are lost. It reads what is set up and what is missing and suggests the next steps with links to the right pages.
headings: How it differs from the page chat

docs.title: Playground: worlds and scenarios
docs.summary: The playground drops agents into a simulated world and runs it tick by tick, so you can watch behaviour rather than read about it.

docs.title: Projects
docs.summary: A project is one codebase or one effort inside a workspace. It gives work a folder, a structure graph and a task tree.
headings: What a project adds over a bare workspace

docs.title: Project deployments
docs.summary: A project's frontend and backend run from inside the hub: deployed, watched, restarted, shown in the dashboard, shared through /apps/<slug>/ and opened by the agent's own browser.

docs.title: Scheduling and the Plan page
docs.summary: Future work: notifications, agent tasks, flow and loop triggers, plus the inbox showing what fired.

docs.title: Proactive agents
docs.summary: An agent with a pulse of its own: it wakes up on a schedule, checks its sources, acts within a budget, writes to you only when it has something to say, and remembers between ticks what it saw.

docs.title: Watchers
docs.summary: Observers of outside state (a mailbox over IMAP, an HTTP resource) that poll on their own interval and wake a proactive agent when something changes, without running a model.

docs.title: Service health and diagnostics
docs.summary: Whether the moving parts are alive, and what to do when they are not.

docs.title: Runbook: typical failures
docs.summary: Symptom, how to confirm it and the fix for the failures operators hit most: an invalid or rate limited provider key, a model not enabled, no docker daemon, no worker so runs stay pending, a locked SQLite or unreachable Postgres, migrations failing at start or a database written by a newer release, a disk full of run logs, a budget refusal, a stuck lease, an MCP handshake failure, SSE buffered by a proxy and a widget CORS refusal; plus ah support-bundle, the zip of version, doctor, health, migrations, masked config, recent errors, log tails and SLO status with every secret scrubbed.
headings: Provider key invalid or rate limited
Worker not running: runs stay pending

docs.title: SLO: run start time and error rate
docs.summary: Two service level objectives over a rolling hour: run start p95 (recorded to started, agent and entity runs) under AGENTS_HUB_SLO_START_P95_SECONDS (30 s) and the share of finished runs that failed under AGENTS_HUB_SLO_ERROR_RATE (5%, at least 20 runs). GET /api/support/slo and the Health page card show them; /metrics exports agents_hub_run_start_seconds and agents_hub_slo_breach; deploy/prometheus/alerts.yml and an optional Helm PrometheusRule alert on them; notification rules slo_start_latency and slo_error_rate fire once on a breach and once on recovery.

docs.title: Sessions and runs
docs.summary: These two records are how everything in the product becomes observable. Why a run failed: its status, error and log, and what a stale run means.

docs.title: Settings
docs.summary: Credentials and connection details. What models are offered and which is default lives on the [models](models.md) page, not here.

docs.title: Skills
docs.summary: Reusable procedures agents follow: steps or Markdown instructions, attached per agent, versioned with history, restore and pinning, installed copies that know when their original moved on, skills synced from any SKILL.md folder of a project repository, public skill sources connected in one click, a safety review with flags, scripts and the license verdict on every imported skill, SKILL.md import and export.
headings: The part that trips everyone up

docs.title: System agents
docs.summary: An agent is either **system** (shipped with the product) or **custom** (yours). There is nothing in between.
headings: What being a system agent means
Why the last two are separate

docs.title: Tasks
docs.summary: A task is tracked work: it has a status, an owner, subtasks, dependencies, and a result that outlives the conversation that produced it.

docs.title: Issue trackers
docs.summary: Jira and Linear are linked to a project's repository. A sync is idempotent: issues from the tracker become tasks. Tools read issues, create them, comment and transition their status.

docs.title: Teams
docs.summary: A team is a bounded roster of agents that know each other and work over a shared message board.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.summary: A Telegram bot can be bound to this service, so a conversation continues from a phone and notifications arrive where you are.

docs.title: Tools and capabilities
docs.summary: Tools are granted to an agent by name. Nothing is granted by default, including the calculator. The browser tools (Playwright in its own container, browser_open, browser_read, browser_act, browser_screenshot) and run_code (a sandboxed code interpreter in a throwaway container) live here too.
headings: Why capabilities and not tool names
Delegation counts as holding the capability
Approval gates, which are a different thing

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.summary: Symptoms in the order people hit them: runs that will not start, output that never appears, numbers that look wrong, Docker, and the CLI.

docs.title: Views and Studio
docs.summary: A view is something an agent built to be looked at: a chart, a graph, a table, a 3D scene, a simulation, a slide deck (with layouts, themes, PDF and PowerPoint export) or a document.

docs.title: Web requests
docs.summary: Every `web_search` and `fetch_url` call an agent made, recorded with the text it was actually handed. The **Web Requests** page is where you read them.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.summary: A workspace is the unit of isolation: its own folder on disk, its own roster of agents, its own settings, its own memory pools and its own projects.

docs.title: Workspace roles
docs.summary: A role is a kind of work (coder, reviewer, web search, visualizer and more) and each workspace says which of its agents does it. System agents call @coder rather than swe_agent, so swapping in Claude Code, Codex or Aider is one setting.

docs.title: Special models
docs.summary: Models for images, video, speech, transcription and a workspace's own models, added per workspace with no fallback except a personal workspace, which uses default's. Agents call generate_image, generate_video, synthesize_speech, transcribe_audio or ask_special_model; a purpose with no model answers model_not_added; results are saved as workspace files and priced against the run's money cap.
docs.surface: Models, Special models tab; Workspace settings, Special models section

docs.title: Notifications
docs.summary: Outbound webhooks and Slack endpoints, alert rules for a failed run, spend past a threshold or a low online eval score, and the signed, idempotent inbound webhooks (the node runner, a flow trigger, and filing a task from outside).

docs.title: Running more than one backend
docs.summary: docker compose --scale backend=N needs the cross-replica broker bridge (AGENTS_HUB_BROKER_URL, a Redis Stream that also lets a browser reconnecting to another replica catch up by Last-Event-ID) or SSE clients pinned to another replica stop seeing live updates; AGENTS_HUB_DATABASE_URL puts the database in Postgres (ah db migrate moves an existing one); AGENTS_HUB_ROLE=api plus ah worker runs agents on other hosts (workers.md); the default single replica on SQLite needs none of this.

docs.title: Identity
docs.summary: Who is using this hub and what they may do. Three modes set with `AUTH_MODE`: a single operator (the default, no login at all), a shared API token, or named users with passwords, roles and per-workspace membership.
headings: Roles and what each may do
How passwords and sessions are stored

docs.title: Integrations
docs.summary: External services agents read from and write to: Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar), Microsoft Graph (Outlook Calendar), and future connectors for Notion, Confluence and databases.

docs.title: A2A (Agent2Agent)
docs.summary: A2A is the open protocol for one agent to call another across products: a JSON Agent Card at a well-known URL, and JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. The hub speaks it both ways, serving a card for every agent and importing an agent from nothing but its card URL.

docs.title: Roles, workers and the launch queue
docs.summary: AGENTS_HUB_ROLE splits one process into an api backend that queues launches and ah worker processes that spawn them on any host; runs report a heartbeat instead of a pid, write a checkpoint after every tool call and are resumed from it, and singletons (scheduler, watchdog, Telegram, outbox) run under database leases.

docs.title: Files and the object store
docs.summary: AGENTS_HUB_BLOB_URL (an s3://bucket/prefix, optionally with AGENTS_HUB_BLOB_ENDPOINT for MinIO) mirrors run logs, node logs, flow logs and view assets into an object store via common/blobs.py, so a backend replica or worker on another host can read a file it did not write; empty (default) keeps every read and write local, exactly as before.
headings: What still needs a shared mount

docs.title: Deploying for high availability
docs.summary: Every shape the service runs in, smallest first: the single-user quickstart from the published images, compose from a checkout, the postgres, scale and browser profiles, the compose ha profile and the Helm chart. Then the ha profile and the chart in detail: the compose ha profile (postgres, redis, a bundled minio, backend-api and worker replicas) and a Helm chart for a real cluster, both wiring up the api/worker split from workers.md and the broker bridge and Postgres from scaling.md into something runnable; the shared .agents_hub/ files are the remaining one-host (or one-ReadWriteMany-volume) limit until AGENTS_HUB_BLOB_URL moves them to an object store. The Cluster page (GET /api/cluster) and ah deployment show the map: members with their heartbeat, load and leases, the queue, and runs, loops, resident instances and containers by host, with each process's own log. Releases are one semver version across pyproject, the dashboard, the Helm chart, the images and a vX.Y.Z tag: scripts/release.py cuts them, the release workflow publishes images to GHCR, and a rollback over a release with migrations restores the pre-migrate archive a SQLite database takes by itself before it migrates.

docs.title: Backup and recovery
docs.summary: ah db backup writes one archive (a self-contained SQLite file plus, by default, the state directories beside it); ah db restore loads it back; ah db verify checks it without touching the live database.

docs.title: SCIM provisioning
docs.summary: The channel an identity provider drives itself: /scim/v2 implements SCIM 2.0 Users and Groups (filtering, paging, PATCH) so Entra ID, Okta or Keycloak can create, rename and deactivate accounts here directly, gated by AUTH_SCIM_TOKEN.
headings: Groups become hub groups, and mappings give them meaning

docs.title: Single sign-on
docs.summary: Sign in with Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or any OpenID Connect provider (Authorization Code with PKCE). Groups from the id token become global roles and workspace memberships through mapping rules on the Accounts page.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.summary: Encrypted per-workspace values, optionally scoped to one agent or one user, handed to a run as environment variables only under the names its agent declares.

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.summary: Who did what, when, to which object: the append-only trail (token and multi mode) written by the write-request middleware and by key points across the hub (login, run launch, tool approval, workspace policy, env and budget), readable by an administrator in full or by anyone else for their own actions and the workspaces they own, exportable as CSV or JSONL, and offered to audit-subscribed webhooks.

docs.title: Personal API keys
docs.summary: A key one person cuts for themselves under AUTH_MODE=multi: acts as its owner, never wider, optionally scoped to workspaces and an expiry. Used by the CLI over AGENTS_HUB_URL, an A2A client talking to another hub, and CI. Managed on the Account page.

docs.title: GitHub App
docs.summary: The hub holds a GitHub App and issues GitHub tokens itself: an installation token for the workspace an installation is bound to (pull requests come from the app's bot) and a user token for each person who connected their GitHub account (pull requests come from them), handed to runs whose agent declares GITHUB_TOKEN when no explicit secret supplies one.
docs.surface: Connectors, Git, GitHub App card; Account, Connected accounts
headings: Installing and binding to a workspace

docs.title: The system workspace
docs.summary: A workspace where the service looks after itself: a git copy of this repository under the state directory, a doctor agent that files [system] tasks and an engineer agent that proposes fixes as system/ branches of the copy. A scheduled maintenance loop, paused by default, never pushes; a human fetches and pushes.
headings: When the service runs in docker

docs.title: The demo workspace
docs.summary: A workspace called demo, seeded end to end: a small sample web shop, three custom agents, a flow, a team, a scenario, views, tasks in every status and a couple of recorded chats. Turned on with --with-demo or a Settings toggle.

docs.title: Local models
docs.summary: Managing local model servers from the hub: an external Ollama (pull, list, delete, disk size) and the hub's own runtime under deploy/models (llama.cpp server, downloads from Hugging Face, load and unload, memory), registered as the provider hub-local.

docs.title: The hub as a provider
docs.summary: The hub serves an OpenAI-compatible /v1 (models, chat completions with streaming) so external clients can call any model the catalog enables through one address, authorised by personal API keys, with tokens counted and every call in the audit log.

docs.title: Model structure
docs.summary: A read-only view of a local model's structure from its GGUF or safetensors header without loading the weights: architecture, layers, tensors and memory, drawn as a 2D block diagram or a 3D stack, and a card for API models.

docs.title: The browser
docs.summary: The agent's browser on screen: a live view of a run's browser session with the option to take control, and a free browsing page whose session can be handed to an agent. Built on the same browser service the browser tools use, under the same domain policy.
headings: Handing a page to an agent

docs.title: Terminal
docs.summary: A shell in a running container from the dashboard: a Docker run's container from the run page, a service replica's container from its row. Opened with a one-time ticket over a WebSocket; the hub keeps the shell through a dropped socket for a grace period and replays recent output on reconnect. Owner or admin only, audited on open and close.

docs.title: Tool policy
docs.summary: Three modes decide what an agent's tool call can do: always_allow runs it, always_ask holds it for approval, and auto sends it to a small model to classify.
headings: What happens to a denied call

docs.title: Outcomes
docs.summary: A task can have an outcome: a markdown rubric that defines done, with max attempts, an optional grader model and an optional pass threshold.

docs.title: Steering
docs.summary: Send a message to a running run while it is still working, either injected into the conversation stream or interrupting it to restart on a new task.

docs.title: Agent loop
docs.summary: What happens between a run's model calls and the policies inside it: steering, compaction, tool search, structured output and fallback models, with guardrails and the tool policy around them, their agent and workspace settings, and the loop block a run records.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.summary: Workspace or global checks on a run's input and final answer, by a rule (regex, keywords, PII, length) or a judge model, that block the run or warn, with an event log and audit records.

docs.title: Chat widget
docs.summary: A chat bubble for your own website: one script tag talking to one agent of a workspace, with conversations kept on the hub, streamed replies and attachments, guarded by a publishable key, an origin allowlist, signed visitor tokens and per-widget limits.
headings: What the visitor sees, and what they do not

docs.title: Consent portal
docs.summary: A widget visitor or chat channel user grants an agent their own Google or Microsoft account through a public consent page: a signed single use link, the provider's sign in with offline access, the refresh token kept as their personal secret, the agent's Google and Outlook tools acting only as them in their own turns, and revoke by the person or the operator.
headings: How it works in a turn

docs.title: Handoffs
docs.summary: Give a chat conversation to another agent: targets, history filters (full, summary, last_n, none), limits, events, and handoff versus delegation.

docs.title: Sandboxes
docs.summary: Where run_code and the Chat code panel run snippets: docker, local, e2b or modal, chosen per environment or by CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER, with each provider's network policy and the enforced docker network that has no route out except the egress proxy.
headings: The `run_code` tool and the code view

docs.title: Isolated workspaces
docs.summary: A workspace as a perimeter: shell and code run in a sandbox container with no network, only an allowlist of tools that stay inside, the internet readable only on the workspace's own list of sites (GET only, read only browser), and every hub way out (MCP, channels, widgets, webhooks, personal memory, hook files) closed.

docs.title: Workspace files
docs.summary: Files uploaded once and referenced by id in chat, memory, tasks and evals, plus numbered RAG citations in answers.

docs.title: TypeScript SDK
docs.summary: A typed client for an Agents Hub from outside it: clients/agents-hub-ts, generated types from the hub's own OpenAPI schema plus a hand-written layer for agents, tasks, chat (with streaming) and the /v1 OpenAI compatible endpoints.
headings: What is generated, what is hand-written

docs.title: Changelog: what's new in each release
docs.summary: What changed in every release, newest first: features added, behaviour changed, bugs fixed, security notes and upgrade notes. The place to find the latest, recent and new functionality of the service.
